questions.text: If the prime factorisation of 2520 is $2^3 \times 3^a \times b \times 7$, then the value of $a + 2b$ is:
If $a$ is a non-zero rational and $\sqrt{b}$ is irrational, then $a\sqrt{b}$ is:
questions.answer: (d) an irrational number — if possible let $a\sqrt b = \frac{p}{q}$ be rational; then $\sqrt b = \frac{p}{aq}$ is rational, a contradiction. Hence $a\sqrt b$ is irrational.

questions.text: If $\alpha,\beta$ are zeroes of a polynomial $p(x) = 2x^2 - x - 1$ then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to
questions.answer: (b) $\frac{5}{4}$ — $\alpha+\beta=\frac12$, $\alpha\beta=-\frac12$; $\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=\frac14+1=\frac54$.

questions.text: It is given that the difference between the zeros of $4x^2 - 8kx + 9$ is 4 and $k > 0$. Then, $k = ?$
questions.answer: (c) $\frac{5}{2}$ — $\alpha+\beta=2k$, $\alpha\beta=\frac94$, $\alpha-\beta=4$. $(\alpha+\beta)^2=(\alpha-\beta)^2+4\alpha\beta \Rightarrow 4k^2=16+9=25 \Rightarrow k=\pm\frac52$; since $k>0$, $k=\frac52$.

questions.text: If 18th and 11th terms of an A.P. are in the ratio $3:2$, then its 21st and 5th terms are in the ratio
questions.answer: (a) $3:1$ — $\frac{a+17d}{a+10d}=\frac32\Rightarrow 2a+34d=3a+30d\Rightarrow a=4d$. $\frac{a_{21}}{a_5}=\frac{a+20d}{a+4d}=\frac{24d}{8d}=\frac31$.

questions.text: $\triangle ABC$ is such that $AB = 3$ cm, $BC = 2$ cm and $CA = 2.5$ cm. If $\triangle DEF \sim \triangle ABC$ and $EF = 4$ cm, then perimeter of $\triangle DEF$ is
questions.answer: (d) 15 cm — $\frac{AB}{DE}=\frac{BC}{EF}\Rightarrow\frac{3}{DE}=\frac24\Rightarrow DE=6$ cm; $\frac{2.5}{DF}=\frac24\Rightarrow DF=5$ cm. Perimeter $=6+4+5=15$ cm.

questions.text: In what ratio does x-axis divide the line segment joining the points $A(2, -3)$ and $B(5, 6)$?
questions.answer: (d) $1:2$ — let the x-axis cut AB in ratio $k:1$; $y=\frac{6k-3}{k+1}=0\Rightarrow k=\frac12$, so the ratio is $1:2$.

questions.text: The value of $\left(\frac{1}{\sec^2 A}+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}^2 A}\right)$ is:
If $\sin A = \frac23$, then value of $\cot A$ is:

questions.text: AP and PQ are tangents drawn from a point A to a circle with centre O and radius 9 cm. If $OA = 15$ cm, then $AP + AQ =$
questions.answer: (d) 24 cm — $OP\perp AP$, so $AP^2=15^2-9^2=144$, $AP=12$ cm; $AP=AQ=12$ cm (tangents from A), so $AP+AQ=24$ cm.

questions.text: A solid consists of a circular cylinder with an exact fitting right circular cone placed at the top. The height of the cone is $h$. If the total volume of the solid is 3 times the volume of the cone, then the height of the circular cylinder is
questions.answer: (b) $\frac{2h}{3}$ — $\pi r^2h_1+\frac13\pi r^2h=3\cdot\frac13\pi r^2h=\pi r^2h\Rightarrow h_1=h-\frac h3=\frac{2h}{3}$.

questions.text: Two friends were born in the year 1996. The probability that they have the same birth date is
questions.answer: (a) $\frac{1}{366}$ — 1996 was a leap year (366 days); favourable outcomes = 1, so probability $=\frac1{366}$.

questions.text: Prove that $5\sqrt2 - 3$ is an irrational number, given that $\sqrt2$ is an irrational number.
questions.answer: Assume $x=5\sqrt2-3$ is rational. Then $\sqrt2=\frac{x+3}{5}$ is rational (RHS is rational), which contradicts the fact that $\sqrt2$ is irrational. Hence our assumption is wrong and $5\sqrt2-3$ is irrational.

questions.text:
Is the pair of linear equations consistent? Justify your answer.
$2ax + by = a,\ 4ax + 2by - 2a = 0;\ a, b \neq 0$
questions.answer: Yes. Here $a_1=2a, b_1=b, c_1=-a$ and $a_2=4a, b_2=2b, c_2=-2a$. $\frac{a_1}{a_2}=\frac{b_1}{b_2}=\frac{c_1}{c_2}=\frac12$, so the pair has infinitely many solutions (coincident lines), i.e. it is consistent (dependent).

questions.text: Find the co-ordinates of the points of trisection of the line segment joining the points $(-2, 2)$ and $(7, -4)$.
questions.answer: Let P, Q trisect AB with A(-2,2), B(7,-4). $AP:PB=1:2$, so $P=\left(\frac{7-4}{3},\frac{-4+4}{3}\right)=(1,0)$. $AQ:QB=2:1$, so $Q=\left(\frac{14-2}{3},\frac{-8+2}{3}\right)=(4,-2)$.

questions.text: Prove that: $1+\frac{\cot^2\theta}{1+\operatorname{cosec}\theta}=\operatorname{cosec}\theta$
questions.answer: LHS $=1+\frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta-1}{1+\operatorname{cosec}\theta}=1+\frac{(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1)}{1+\operatorname{cosec}\theta}=1+\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1=\operatorname{cosec}\theta=$ RHS.

questions.text:
A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of playing cards. Find the probability of drawing
i. a face card
ii. a red face card.
questions.answer: $n(S)=52$. Face cards $=4\times3=12$; red face cards $=3\times2=6$. (i) $P=\frac{12}{52}=\frac{3}{13}$. (ii) $P=\frac{6}{52}=\frac{3}{26}$.

questions.text: The area of a rectangle gets reduced by $8\ \mathrm{m}^2$, when its length is reduced by 5 m and its breadth is increased by 3 m. If we increase the length by 3 m and breadth by 2 m, the area is increased by $74\ \mathrm{m}^2$. Find the length and the breadth of the rectangle.
questions.answer: Let length $=x$ m, breadth $=y$ m. $xy-(x-5)(y+3)=8\Rightarrow 3x-5y=7$ ... (i). $(x+3)(y+2)-xy=74\Rightarrow 2x+3y=68$ ... (ii). Multiplying (i) by 3 and (ii) by 5: $9x-15y=21$, $10x+15y=340$; adding, $19x=361\Rightarrow x=19$. Then $y=\frac{171-21}{15}=10$. Length = 19 m, breadth = 10 m.

or.text: A man sold a chair and a table together for ₹1520 thereby making a profit of 25% on the chair and 10% on table. By selling them together for ₹1535 he would have made a profit of 10% on the chair and 25% on the table. Find the cost price of each.
or.answer: Let cost prices of chair and table be ₹$x$ and ₹$y$. $\frac{125}{100}x+\frac{110}{100}y=1520\Rightarrow 25x+22y=30400$ ... (i). $\frac{110}{100}x+\frac{125}{100}y=1535\Rightarrow 22x+25y=30700$ ... (ii). (ii) − (i): $x-y=-100$ ... (iii). (i) + (ii): $x+y=1300$ ... (iv). Solving, $x=600$, $y=700$. Cost price of chair = ₹600 and of table = ₹700.

questions.text: Prove that the points $(2, 3)$, $(-4, -6)$ and $(1, 3/2)$ do not form a triangle.
questions.answer: Let A(2,3), B(-4,-6), C(1,3/2). $AB=\sqrt{36+81}=\sqrt{117}$; $BC=\sqrt{25+\frac{225}{4}}=\sqrt{81.25}$; $AC=\sqrt{1+\frac94}=\sqrt{3.25}$. Since $AC+BC=AB$ (the sum of two sides is not greater than the third), A, B, C are collinear and do not form a triangle.

questions.text: Prove that: $(\sin\theta + 1 + \cos\theta)(\sin\theta - 1 + \cos\theta)\cdot\sec\theta\operatorname{cosec}\theta = 2$
questions.answer: LHS $=[(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2-1]\cdot\frac1{\cos\theta\sin\theta}=[1+2\sin\theta\cos\theta-1]\cdot\frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=2=$ RHS.

questions.text: In the given figure, E is a point on side CB produced of an isosceles $\triangle ABC$ with $AB = AC$. If $AD \perp BC$ and $EF \perp AC$, Prove that $\triangle ABD \sim \triangle ECF$.
questions.answer: Since $AB=AC$, $\angle B=\angle C$. In $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ECF$: $\angle B=\angle C$ and $\angle ADB=\angle EFC=90^\circ$. Hence $\triangle ABD\sim\triangle ECF$ by AA similarity.

or.text: P and Q are points on the sides AB and AC respectively of a $\triangle ABC$. If $AP = 2$ cm, $PB = 4$ cm, $AQ = 3$ cm and $QC = 6$ cm, show that $BC = 3PQ$.
or.answer: $AB=6$ cm, $AC=9$ cm. $\frac{AP}{PB}=\frac24=\frac12$ and $\frac{AQ}{QC}=\frac36=\frac12$, so $\frac{AP}{PB}=\frac{AQ}{QC}$; also $\angle A=\angle A$. So $\triangle APQ\sim\triangle ABC$ (SAS) and $\frac{AP}{AB}=\frac{PQ}{BC}=\frac{AQ}{AC}\Rightarrow\frac{PQ}{BC}=\frac39=\frac13\Rightarrow BC=3PQ$.

questions.text: A momento is made as shown in the figure. Its base PBCR is silver plated from the front side. Find the area which is silver plated. ($\pi=\frac{22}{7}$)
questions.answer: Base $=7+3=10$ cm, height $=7+3=10$ cm. Area of right-angled $\triangle ABC=\frac12\times10\times10=50\ \mathrm{cm}^2$. Area of quadrant APR $=\frac14\times\frac{22}{7}\times49=38.5\ \mathrm{cm}^2$. Silver plated area = area of PBCR $=50-38.5=11.5\ \mathrm{cm}^2$.

questions.text: In the given figure, PA and PB are two tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O. If $\angle PBA = 65^\circ$, find $\angle OAB$ and $\angle APB$.
questions.answer: $PA=PB$ (tangents from P), so $\angle PAB=\angle PBA=65^\circ$. $\angle APB=180^\circ-(65^\circ+65^\circ)=50^\circ$. $OA\perp AP$, so $\angle OAP=90^\circ$ and $\angle OAB=90^\circ-65^\circ=25^\circ$. Hence $\angle OAB=25^\circ$, $\angle APB=50^\circ$.

questions.text: The difference of squares of two numbers is 204. The square of the smaller number is 4 less than 10 times the larger number. Find the two numbers.
questions.answer: Let the numbers be $x$ (larger) and $y$. $x^2-y^2=204$ ... (i); $y^2=10x-4$ ... (ii). From (i),(ii): $x^2-10x+4-204=0\Rightarrow x^2-10x-200=0\Rightarrow(x-20)(x+10)=0$; $x=20$ (reject $x=-10$). Then $y^2=196$, $y=14$. The numbers are 20 and 14.

or.text: The denominator of a fraction is 2 more than the numerator. If 2 is added to both its numerator and denominator, then the sum of the new fraction and the original fraction is $\frac{46}{35}$. Find the original fraction.
or.answer: Let the fraction be $\frac{x}{x+2}$. $\frac{x}{x+2}+\frac{x+2}{x+4}=\frac{46}{35}\Rightarrow 24x^2+4x-228=0$, i.e. $6x^2+x-57=0\Rightarrow(6x+19)(x-3)=0$. $x\neq-\frac{19}{6}$, so $x=3$. The fraction is $\frac35$.

questions.text: The $16^{\text{th}}$ term of an AP is 5 times its $3^{\text{rd}}$ term. If its $10^{\text{th}}$ term is 41, find the sum of its first 15 terms.
questions.answer: $a_{16}=5a_3\Rightarrow a+15d=5a+10d\Rightarrow 4a=5d$ ... (i). $a_{10}=41\Rightarrow a+9d=41\Rightarrow4a+36d=164\Rightarrow5d+36d=164\Rightarrow d=4$, $a=5$. $S_{15}=\frac{15}{2}[2(5)+14(4)]=\frac{15}{2}\times66=495$.

questions.text: A statue 1.6 m tall, stands on the top of a pedestal. From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the statue is $60^\circ$ and from the same point the angle of elevation of the top of the pedestal is $45^\circ$. Find the height of the pedestal. (Use $\sqrt3=1.732$)
questions.answer: Let AB = statue (1.6 m), BC = pedestal, D the point on ground. In $\triangle BCD$: $\tan45^\circ=\frac{BC}{CD}\Rightarrow CD=BC$. In $\triangle ACD$: $\tan60^\circ=\frac{AB+BC}{CD}\Rightarrow\sqrt3\,BC=1.6+BC\Rightarrow0.73\,BC=1.6$ (using 1.73) $\Rightarrow BC=\frac{1.6}{0.73}\approx2.19$ m.

or.text: A spherical balloon of radius $r$ subtends an angle of $60^\circ$ at the eye of an observer. If the angle of elevation of its centre is $45^\circ$ from the same point, then prove that height of the centre of the balloon is $\sqrt2$ times its radius.
or.answer: Let B be the observer; $\angle QBP=60^\circ$, $\angle ABO=45^\circ$. $\angle PBO=\frac12\times60^\circ=30^\circ$. $\sin30^\circ=\frac{r}{OB}=\frac12\Rightarrow OB=2r$. $\sin45^\circ=\frac{OA}{OB}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\Rightarrow OB=\sqrt2\,OA$. So $OA=\frac{2r}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2\,r$, i.e. height of centre $=\sqrt2\,r$.

questions.text: A wooden toy is shown in the picture. This is a cuboidal wooden block of dimensions $14\text{ cm}\times17\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$. On its top there are seven cylindrical hollows for bees to fit in. Each cylindrical hollow is of height 3 cm and radius 2 cm.

subparts.text: Find the volume of wood carved out to make one cylindrical hollow.
Find the lateral surface area of the cuboid to paint it with green colour.
Find the volume of wood in the remaining cuboid after carving out seven cylindrical hollows.
subparts.answer: Volume of 7 hollows $=264\ \mathrm{cm}^3$. Volume of cuboid $=14\times17\times4=952\ \mathrm{cm}^3$. Remaining volume $=952-264=688\ \mathrm{cm}^3$.

questions.text:
Teaching Mathematics through activities is a powerful approach that enhances students' understanding and engagement. Keeping this in mind, Ms. Mukta planned a prime number game for class 5 students. She announces the number 2 in her class and asked the first student to multiply it by a prime number and then pass it to second student. Second student also multiplied it by a prime number and passed it to third student. In this way by multiplying to a prime number, the last student got 173250.
Now, Mukta asked some questions as given below to the students:

subparts.text: What is the least prime number used by students?
How many students are in the class?
subparts.answer: $173250=2\times5^3\times3^2\times7\times11$. Number of students in the class $=3+2+1+1=7$.

or.text: What is the highest prime number used by students?
